Guardrails.Core.Graph;\n\nnamespace Guardrails.Core.Tests;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// Unit tests for <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render\"/> (issue #33): the self-contained local\n/// <c>diagram.html</c> viewer. Pure string mapping — no disk. Pins the provenance line, the\n/// verbatim-source embedding, the interaction prerequisites (loose security for clicks, pan/zoom,\n/// fullscreen), determinism, and newline normalization.\n/// </summary>\npublic sealed class HtmlDiagramRendererTests\n{\n    private const string Hash = \"abc123def456\";\n    private const string Source = \"flowchart TD\\n  task_a[\\\"a\\\"]:::task\\n  classDef task fill:#cfe8ff;\";\n\n    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> NoTargets =\n        new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);\n\n    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> OneTarget =\n        new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal) { [\"task_01_a\"] = \"tasks/01-a/\" };\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_FirstLine_IsProvenanceComment_WithSameHash()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n        string firstLine = html.Split('\\n')[0];\n\n        // Same provenance shape as diagram.md, and FIRST so the \\A-anchored reader (graph --check)\n        // matches it in both files.\n        Assert.Equal($\"<!-- guardrails:graph v1 source-sha256={Hash} -->\", firstLine);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EmbedsSourceVerbatim_InRawTextScript()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"type=\\\"text/plain\\\"\", html);\n        Assert.Contains(Source, html); // verbatim — not interpolated into a JS string\n        Assert.Contains(\"<!doctype html>\", html);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EnablesClicksAndNavigation()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        // Clicks (node -> source file) only fire when mermaid runs in 'loose' security.\n        Assert.Contains(\"securityLevel: 'loose'\", html);\n        // Pan/zoom + fullscreen affordances.\n        Assert.Contains(\"svg-pan-zoom\", html);\n        Assert.Contains(\"requestFullscreen\", html);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_RaisesMermaidSizeCeilings_SoLargeDagsRender()\n    {\n        // Issue #108: a large plan's DAG source exceeds Mermaid's default 50 000-char maxTextSize\n        // and/or 500-edge maxEdges ceiling, so mermaid.render throws and the page falls back to\n        // \"could not render\". The fix lifts BOTH ceilings in mermaid.initialize — assert they are\n        // present (a regression that drops either re-introduces the big-plan render failure).\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"maxTextSize: 5000000\", html);\n        Assert.Contains(\"maxEdges: 100000\", html);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_IsDeterministic()\n    {\n        Assert.Equal(\n            HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget),\n            HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget));\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_NormalizesCrlf_NoCarriageReturnsInOutput()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(\"flowchart TD\\r\\n  a-->b\\r\\n\", Hash, NoTargets);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain('\\r', html);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EmptyHash_Throws()\n    {\n        Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, \"\", NoTargets));\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_NullTaskFolderTargets_Throws()\n    {\n        Assert.Throws<ArgumentNullException>(() => HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, null!));\n    }\n\n    // === legend overlay (outside the Mermaid graph; see MermaidRenderer remarks) =======\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_IncludesALegendOverlayDiv_OutsideTheEmbeddedMermaidSource()\n    {\n        // A Mermaid-native legend was prototyped and rendered broken headless (dagre treats a\n        // disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra \"task\"); the only working placement is an HTML\n        // overlay div outside the embedded Mermaid <script> source, mirroring #bar/#hint.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"legend\\\"\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_LegendOverlay_StatesBothAColorAndABeforeAfterTimingWord()\n    {\n        // A bare category name would not preserve the \"preflights run before, guardrails run\n        // after\" semantic the removed nested boxes used to convey visually — the legend must spell\n        // out both the colour mapping AND the timing/consequence in words.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"Preflight\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"Guardrail\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"BEFORE\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"AFTER\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_LegendOverlay_IsNotInsideTheEmbeddedGraphSourceScript()\n    {\n        // The legend must live OUTSIDE the raw-text <script id=\"graph-source\"> element — it is\n        // not part of the Mermaid source, so it can never affect anything that parses that source\n        // (rendering) or hashes it (GraphSourceHash, via MermaidRenderer.SemanticContent).\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        int scriptStart = html.IndexOf(\"id=\\\"graph-source\\\"\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int scriptEnd = html.IndexOf(\"</script>\", scriptStart, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        string scriptContent = html[scriptStart..scriptEnd];\n\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"legend\", scriptContent, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    // === task-container title-band overlay (issue #232/#233 superseded, issue #235) ====\n    //\n    // The Mermaid-source anchor-node mechanism (#211) proved useless in practice — a real\n    // headless-Chrome measurement found the anchor covering only 0.44% of a content-dense\n    // container's area, off-center, missed by every realistic click point. The fix instead\n    // injects a post-render SVG overlay on the container's title/label band via JavaScript.\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EmbedsTaskFolderTargets_AsJsonSideTable()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"task-folder-targets\\\"\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"\\\"task_01_a\\\"\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"tasks/01-a/\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_NoLongerEmitsAnchorNodeMechanism()\n    {\n        // The #211 anchor-node click mechanism (Mermaid-source invisible node + classDef) is\n        // superseded entirely — HtmlDiagramRenderer must not reference it either.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"classDef invisible\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_AppendsToCluster_NotInsertsFirst()\n    {\n        // Load-bearing z-order fix: appendChild (not insertBefore as firstChild) — see class\n        // remarks and HtmlDiagramRenderer's remarks for why insertBefore silently blocks clicks\n        // (it lands the overlay BEHIND the cluster's own background rect).\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"cluster.appendChild(a)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"insertBefore(a, cluster.firstChild\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_ComputesBandFromClusterAndLabelBBox()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"cluster.getBBox()\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"label.getBBox()\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\".cluster-label\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_UsesTransparentFill_NotNone()\n    {\n        // Same hit-testing hazard as the retired anchor node: fill:none is invisible to\n        // pointer-events:visiblePainted hit-testing; the overlay rect must use a painted-but-\n        // invisible transparent fill instead.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"'transparent'\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_SetsFillViaInlineStyle_NotTheFillAttribute()\n    {\n        // Real-browser regression (found live, not guessed): Mermaid's own generated stylesheet\n        // carries a rule shaped like `#dag .cluster rect{fill:<theme color>;...}`. Since the\n        // overlay rect is nested inside the .cluster group, that selector matches it too — and a\n        // CSS class/tag selector beats a plain HTML presentation attribute, so\n        // `rect.setAttribute('fill', 'transparent')` was silently overridden, painting a solid\n        // theme-colored bar over the container's title text (confirmed via getComputedStyle:\n        // attribute said \"transparent\", computed fill was the theme's cluster-background color).\n        // An inline style (`rect.style.fill = ...`) wins over any external/embedded stylesheet\n        // rule short of `!important`, so it reliably stays invisible. This test would have caught\n        // the regression: `Assert.Contains(\"'transparent'\")` alone passes for EITHER form.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"rect.style.fill = 'transparent'\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"rect.setAttribute('fill'\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_RunsAfterMermaidRenderResolves()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        int renderCall = html.IndexOf(\"await mermaid.render(\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int overlayDefinition = html.IndexOf(\"function addTaskContainerOverlays\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.True(renderCall >= 0 && overlayDefinition >= 0, \"both the render call and overlay function must be present\");\n\n        // The overlay must be INVOKED after the render call (the definition itself may appear\n        // earlier in the script — only invocation order matters for correctness).\n        int overlayInvocation = html.IndexOf(\"addTaskContainerOverlays(\", renderCall, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.True(overlayInvocation > renderCall, \"the overlay must be applied to the SVG mermaid.render just produced\");\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EmptyTaskFolderTargets_StillRendersValidPage()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"task-folder-targets\\\"\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"{}\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    // === long task-name title wrap-overflow fix (issue cluster-label-wrap-overflow) ====\n    //\n    // Mermaid always wraps a cluster's title <div> to a hardcoded 200px width (bundled\n    // mermaid@11.4.1's plain flowchart cluster shape never overrides createText's width=200\n    // default), and dagre's layout pass reserves the container's header-strip height BEFORE that\n    // wrapped height is known — so a long kebab-case task name that wraps to 2+ lines prints past\n    // the reserved strip, overlapping the first leaf guardrail/preflight box below it. No Mermaid\n    // config knob avoids this (verified against the bundled 11.4.1 source). The fix re-wraps the\n    // SAME text at up to the container's own (already wider) width post-render instead, verified\n    // headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names, container widths ~230px-~1100px,\n    // wraps of 2-3 lines): every case converged to one line with the same healthy gap a\n    // never-wrapped label already has, and every already-fits label was left byte-for-byte\n    // unchanged (including the whole golden hello-guardrails example).\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_DefinesFixWrappedClusterLabelsFunction()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"function fixWrappedClusterLabels(svgEl)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_RunsAfterMermaidRenderResolves_AndBeforeTheOverlay()\n    {\n        // Ordering is load-bearing: addTaskContainerOverlays measures the label's CURRENT bbox to\n        // size its click band, so a label the wrap fix already shrank back to one line must be\n        // fixed FIRST, or the band would be sized for the original (possibly multi-line) wrap.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        int renderCall = html.IndexOf(\"await mermaid.render(\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int wrapFixInvocation = html.IndexOf(\"fixWrappedClusterLabels(\", renderCall, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int overlayInvocation = html.IndexOf(\"addTaskContainerOverlays(\", renderCall, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        Assert.True(renderCall >= 0 && wrapFixInvocation > renderCall && overlayInvocation > renderCall,\n            \"both post-render fixes must be invoked after the render call\");\n        Assert.True(wrapFixInvocation < overlayInvocation,\n            \"the wrap fix must run BEFORE the title-band overlay so the band reflects the corrected label size\");\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_MeasuresViaScrollWidth_NotGetBoundingClientRect()\n    {\n        // Regression guard for the exact measurement pitfall this fix's own investigation hit:\n        // getBoundingClientRect() reports on-screen pixels affected by the page's pan-zoom\n        // transform, which is misleading when compared against a foreignObject's local width/\n        // height attributes. scrollWidth/scrollHeight are local layout-box measurements, in the\n        // SAME coordinate system as those attributes, regardless of the current zoom level.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        int fnStart = html.IndexOf(\"function fixWrappedClusterLabels\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int fnEnd = html.IndexOf(\"\\n}\\n\", fnStart, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        string fnBody = html[fnStart..fnEnd];\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"div.scrollWidth\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"div.scrollHeight\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"getBoundingClientRect\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_NeverNarrowsBelowMermaidsOriginalWidth()\n    {\n        // The fix only ever WIDENS a label (fewer lines needs less height, never more) — it must\n        // never choose a width narrower than what Mermaid already assigned, which would be a\n        // regression risking MORE wrapping, not less.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"Math.max(currentWidth, clusterBox.width - 16)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_SkipsLabelsThatAlreadyFitOnOneLine()\n    {\n        // Short names (e.g. every task in the golden hello-guardrails example) must be left\n        // completely untouched — this is the guard that makes that a no-op.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"if (naturalWidth <= currentWidth) continue;\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_RevertsWhenWideningDoesNotReduceHeight()\n    {\n        // A container too narrow to help must fall back to Mermaid's original sizing rather than\n        // risk an oddly-proportioned label — never regress relative to the pre-fix rendering.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"if (newHeight >= currentHeight)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"div.setAttribute('style', savedInline);\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_RecentersTheLabelOnTheSameMidpointAfterWidening()\n    {\n        // Mermaid centers the label group via translate(x - bbox.width / 2, y); widening without\n        // re-centering would shift the (now wider) box off-center over the cluster.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"deltaCenter\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"label.setAttribute('transform',\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    // === live per-node status overlay (issue #219) =====================================\n    //\n    // While a `guardrails run` is in progress, diagram.html gains a small corner-anchored status\n    // badge on each task container, preflight/guardrail leaf, and the plan-level Full Flight Checks\n    // / Terminal Gate brackets: an animated spinner while running, a settled check/X/\"?\" glyph once\n    // finished — driven by an OPTIONAL per-node status map plus an INDEPENDENT includeRefresh\n    // toggle, mirroring LogSiteRenderer.IndexHtml(..., includeRefresh)'s during-run/final duality.\n    //\n    // These tests are structural/string-content assertions over the emitted HTML/JS (no headless\n    // browser is configured in this repo — a documented Level-A gap): they prove the right markup\n    // and data are EMITTED, not that a browser positions the badges pixel-correctly at runtime. The\n    // four non-null-status tests are the intended TDD RED against the throwing stub — the\n    // 02-implement-diagram-status-overlay-renderer task turns them green.\n    //\n    // Status-map ids use the SAME vocabulary MermaidRenderer emits (task containers `task_<base>`,\n    // preflight/guardrail leaves `task_<base>_pf_<n>`/`task_<base>_gr_<n>`, and the two plan-level\n    // brackets `plan_preflights`/`plan_guardrails`) so the post-render overlay script can position a\n    // badge on the matching SVG node. All five status values are exercised.\n    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> SampleStatuses =\n        new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal)\n        {\n            [\"plan_preflights\"] = \"passed\",       // Full Flight Checks bracket (top)\n            [\"task_root\"] = \"running\",            // a task container, mid-run -> spinner\n            [\"task_root_pf_0\"] = \"passed\",        // a preflight leaf check\n            [\"task_root_gr_0\"] = \"failed\",        // a guardrail leaf check\n            [\"task_next\"] = \"pending\",            // a not-yet-started task container\n            [\"plan_guardrails\"] = \"needs-human\",  // Terminal Gate bracket (bottom)\n        };\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithNullNodeStatuses_IsByteIdenticalToCurrentBehavior()\n    {\n        // The static `graph` command path (no live status) must be UNCHANGED by this feature: the\n        // pre-existing three-argument overload and the new call passing nodeStatuses:null must\n        // produce the exact same document, byte-for-byte — the golden fixtures\n        // (examples/hello-guardrails, docs/plans/08-parallel-execution/diagram.html) are out of this\n        // task's scope and must not need regenerating.\n        string legacy = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n        string newNull = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, nodeStatuses: null);\n\n        Assert.Equal(legacy, newNull);\n\n        // ...and the static path carries NONE of the live-overlay markers. Each of these is absent\n        // from today's template, so their absence pins the null path clean — a leak of the feature\n        // into the static path (which would silently change every checked-in diagram.html) fails here.\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", newNull, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"@keyframes\", newNull, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"id=\\\"node-statuses\\\"\", newNull, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithNodeStatuses_EmitsAMetaRefreshTag()\n    {\n        // A non-null status map with the default includeRefresh:true is the DURING-RUN diagram — it\n        // must carry <meta http-equiv=\"refresh\"> so a plain file:// view re-reads itself as the run\n        // progresses (mirrors LogSiteRenderer's during-run index). The static (null) path must not.\n        string live = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses);\n        Assert.Contains(\"<meta http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        string stat = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, nodeStatuses: null);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", stat, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithNodeStatusesAndIncludeRefreshFalse_OmitsTheMetaRefreshTag()\n    {\n        // The FINAL settled render (wired at run-end by 06-wire-diagramobserver-into-runcommand):\n        // nodeStatuses is STILL non-null (every node shows its final settled status) but\n        // includeRefresh:false, so the auto-reload tag is dropped — the page is done refreshing. The\n        // status overlay itself must STILL be emitted (the refresh tag and the overlay are independent).\n        string settled = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(\n            Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses, includeRefresh: false);\n\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", settled, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        // still a live-status document — the overlay data is present regardless of includeRefresh.\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"node-statuses\\\"\", settled, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"\\\"task_root\\\"\", settled, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithNodeStatuses_EmitsAnOverlayForEachStatusEntry()\n    {\n        // Every node id in the status map must be referenced by the overlay-rendering logic — the\n        // map is embedded as a JSON side-table (mirroring the task-folder-targets side-table) keyed\n        // by the SAME Mermaid node/container ids, so the post-render script can position a badge on\n        // each matching SVG node. Assert the QUOTED (JSON-key) form: a bare-word check would false-\n        // positive on ids like `plan_guardrails` that ALREADY appear in a code comment in today's\n        // template — only the emitted status map produces the quoted form.\n        string live = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses);\n\n        foreach (string nodeId in SampleStatuses.Keys)\n        {\n            Assert.Contains($\"\\\"{nodeId}\\\"\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        }\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithRunningStatus_EmitsASpinnerClass_AndSettledStatusesEmitAGlyph()\n    {\n        // \"running\" must render an ANIMATED spinner (a CSS @keyframes rotation — no external\n        // image/GIF dependency), visibly distinct from a settled status's STATIC glyph (check / X /\n        // \"?\"). Assert both the spinner animation + its dedicated class AND at least one settled\n        // glyph are present; the spinner marker (a CSS class) is inherently distinct from the glyph\n        // characters, so a spinner can never be mistaken for a settled state.\n        string live = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses);\n\n        // spinner: a CSS keyframes rotation + a dedicated class (neither exists in the static template).\n        Assert.Contains(\"@keyframes\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"status-spinner\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // settled glyphs: `passed` -> U+2713 CHECK MARK, `failed` -> U+2717 BALLOT X (both present in\n        // SampleStatuses). Written as literal UTF-8 glyphs; this file is valid UTF-8, which Roslyn's\n        // BOM-less source detection decodes as UTF-8, so the literals compile to exactly these chars.\n        Assert.Contains(\"✓\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"✗\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    // === diagram search box (issue #220) ================================================\n    //\n    // A fixed-position #search-box overlay (same technique as #legend/#bar/#hint and the status\n    // badges) sits alongside the live status overlay: a search <input>, a \"N of M\" match counter\n    // with next/prev controls, and client-side JS that substring-matches the typed text against\n    // every Mermaid node's id + visible label, toggles a highlight/dim class per node, and auto\n    // pans/zooms to the first match via the already-loaded svg-pan-zoom instance. UNLIKE the status\n    // overlay, this is unconditional — present regardless of nodeStatuses.\n    //\n    // These are structural/string-content assertions (no headless browser is configured in this\n    // repo — a documented Level-A gap): they prove the right markup/data/script is EMITTED, not\n    // that a browser actually matches, highlights, and pans/zooms at runtime. The search-index side\n    // -table is a deliberate stub (BuildSearchIndexJson always returns \"{}\"), so\n    // Render_SearchScript_ReferencesEveryNodeIdAndLabel is the intended TDD RED against it — the\n    // 08-implement-diagram-search-box task turns it green by parsing the real ids/labels.\n\n    // A realistic sample source (mirrors MermaidRenderer's actual shape: a task container plus a\n    // preflight and a guardrail leaf) with ids/labels distinct enough that a false-positive match\n    // against unrelated template text is implausible.\n    private const string SearchSource = \"\"\"\n        flowchart TD\n          subgraph task_root[\"root-task\"]\n            task_root_pf_0[\"pf-check-one\"]:::preflight\n            task_root_gr_0[\"gr-check-one\"]:::guardrail\n          end\n          style task_root fill:#cfe8ff;\n          classDef preflight fill:#e6d7ff;\n          classDef guardrail fill:#fff3cd;\n        \"\"\";\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_AlwaysEmitsASearchInputElement()\n    {\n        // Unconditional (unlike the status overlay): present whether nodeStatuses is null or not.\n        string withoutStatuses = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n        string withStatuses = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets, SampleStatuses);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"search-input\\\"\", withoutStatuses, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"search-input\\\"\", withStatuses, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_SearchScript_ReferencesEveryNodeIdAndLabel()\n    {\n        // The search-matching data source must actually be POPULATED with the ids and visible\n        // labels a real Mermaid source produces — sliced to the dedicated #search-index side-table\n        // (not a bare page-wide Contains) so this cannot false-positive against the verbatim graph\n        // source, which already contains these same substrings regardless of the search feature.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(SearchSource, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        int indexStart = html.IndexOf(\"id=\\\"search-index\\\"\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.True(indexStart >= 0, \"the #search-index side-table must be present\");\n        int indexEnd = html.IndexOf(\"</script>\", indexStart, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        string indexContent = html[indexStart..indexEnd];\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"task_root\", indexContent, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"root-task\", indexContent, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"task_root_pf_0\", indexContent, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"pf-check-one\", indexContent, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"task_root_gr_0\", indexContent, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"gr-check-one\", indexContent, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_SearchScript_DefinesAHighlightAndDimClass()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\".search-match\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\".search-dim\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_SearchScript_CallsThePanZoomApiForAutoCentering()\n    {\n        // Sliced to the runSearch function BODY (not a bare page-wide Contains) so this cannot\n        // false-positive against a comment merely mentioning pz.pan/pz.zoom above the function —\n        // the stub throws before calling either, so this must fail until the real implementation\n        // actually centers the first match through the pan-zoom instance.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        int fnStart = html.IndexOf(\"function runSearch(\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.True(fnStart >= 0, \"runSearch must be defined\");\n        int fnEnd = html.IndexOf(\"\\n}\\n\", fnStart, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.True(fnEnd > fnStart, \"runSearch's closing brace must be found\");\n        string fnBody = html[fnStart..fnEnd];\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"pz.pan(\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"pz.zoom(\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n}\n","numLines":550,"startLine":1,"totalLines":550}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01RkiRP1seahcbMmp8pNxhei","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tusing System.Text;\n2\tusing Guardrails.Core.Model;\n3\t\n4\tnamespace Guardrails.Core.Graph;\n5\t\n6\t/// <summary>\n7\t/// Renders a plan's task/guardrail DAG as a Mermaid <c>flowchart TD</c> (SSOT §10) using the\n8\t/// CONTAINER model (design-of-record 09-preflight-first-class). Pure: <see cref=\"Render\"/> maps\n9\t/// a <see cref=\"PlanDefinition\"/> to Mermaid text with no I/O.\n10\t/// </summary>\n11\t/// <remarks>\n12\t/// <para>\n13\t/// Shape: each task is a <c>subgraph task_&lt;id&gt;</c> container holding its check nodes\n14\t/// (preflight and guardrail leaves) DIRECTLY inside the container — no nested\n15\t/// <c>Preflights</c>/<c>Guardrails</c> wrapper subgraph, no free guardrail/preflight nodes outside\n16\t/// a container, no per-task <c>done_&lt;id&gt;</c> reconvergence node, no <c>task --&gt; guardrail</c>\n17\t/// fan-out edge. (A per-task nested-subgraph wrapper was tried and dropped — see \"Nested boxes\n18\t/// dropped\" below.) Two mandatory plan-level containers bracket the whole DAG: <c>plan_preflights</c>\n19\t/// (\"Full Flight Checks\") at the top, <c>plan_guardrails</c> (\"Terminal Gate\") at the bottom —\n20\t/// always emitted, even when their folder is empty, because they are structural brackets, not\n21\t/// conditional content. These two stay titled subgraphs (unaffected by the nested-box removal\n22\t/// below): they are one-off heterogeneous brackets on the whole DAG, not a per-task repeated\n23\t/// pattern.\n24\t/// </para>\n25\t/// <para>\n26\t/// <b>Nested boxes dropped (simplification).</b> A task container previously nested a\n27\t/// \"Guardrails\" sub-container (and, when present, a \"Preflights\" sub-container) around its leaf\n28\t/// check nodes — nesting-within-nesting that made a real generated diagram look busy for no\n29\t/// semantic gain: the wrapper subgraph id was never referenced by edge emission, container\n30\t/// styling, or <see cref=\"GraphSourceHash\"/> — purely cosmetic. Leaf check nodes are now emitted\n31\t/// as direct children of the task container; the existing <c>:::preflight</c>/<c>:::guardrail</c>\n32\t/// <c>classDef</c> fill remains the only visual category distinction. Removing the boxes also\n33\t/// removes their visual \"preflights run before, guardrails run after\" cue, so that temporal fact\n34\t/// is now preserved two other ways: (1) a GUARANTEED emission-order contract — a task's preflight\n35\t/// leaf node(s), if any, are always emitted before its guardrail leaf node(s) within the\n36\t/// container (see <see cref=\"AppendTaskContainer\"/>), so position is a stable, tested convention,\n37\t/// not a rendering accident; and (2) the legend (see <see cref=\"LegendMarkdown\"/>) states the\n38\t/// before/after timing in words, not just a bare colour-category name.\n39\t/// </para>\n40\t/// <para>\n41\t/// <b>Legend lives outside the Mermaid graph.</b> A Mermaid-native legend (a disconnected\n42\t/// subgraph of dummy colour-swatch nodes) was prototyped and rendered BROKEN headless against the\n43\t/// exact bundled <c>mermaid@11.4.1</c>: dagre lays out a disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra\n44\t/// \"task\" overlapping the real DAG. The only approach that renders correctly is content OUTSIDE\n45\t/// the Mermaid source entirely: an HTML overlay `&lt;div&gt;` in <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>\n46\t/// for <c>diagram.html</c>, and the shared <see cref=\"LegendMarkdown\"/> block placed by the CLI's\n47\t/// <c>graph</c> command AFTER the fenced <c>```mermaid```</c> block for <c>diagram.md</c> (GitHub's\n48\t/// Mermaid sandbox has no overlay option). Neither destination is part of <see cref=\"Render\"/>'s or\n49\t/// <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/>'s returned Mermaid source, and — same treatment as the existing\n50\t/// cosmetic <c>classDef</c> color lines (added by those two methods, never by\n51\t/// <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/>) — the legend never reaches <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/> either,\n52\t/// so legend-only wording changes never move <see cref=\"GraphSourceHash\"/> and never make\n53\t/// `graph --check` spuriously report a plan stale.\n54\t/// </para>\n55\t/// <para>\n56\t/// <b>Every check node's drawn label is its short, stable <c>Name</c> — never its (possibly long)\n57\t/// <c>Description</c>.</b> A prior version drew a task-level preflight's full descriptive text\n58\t/// (which can run to many words) and truncated it to fit; the owner asked instead for the same\n59\t/// short, meaningful identifier the node's own click target already opens, uniformly for every\n60\t/// check kind at both scopes (issue #222) — so no truncation heuristic is needed anywhere. The\n61\t/// full <see cref=\"GuardrailDefinition.Description\"/> remains reachable via the SAME\n62\t/// <c>click</c>-directive mechanism <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> already uses for every node\n63\t/// (source-file click-through, issue #33) — the tooltip argument of that directive carries the\n64\t/// full text for every check, so no new mechanism was introduced.\n65\t/// </para>\n66\t/// <para>\n67\t/// The DAG is drawn <c>subgraph --&gt; subgraph</c>: each edge references a container's subgraph\n68\t/// id directly (<c>task_A --&gt; task_B</c>, <c>plan_preflights --&gt; task_root</c>, …), so Mermaid\n69\t/// clips the arrow to the container's OUTER BORDER like any ordinary box-to-box flowchart edge —\n70\t/// no interior anchor, no line piercing the box (issue #210). The bundled Mermaid version\n71\t/// (<c>mermaid@11.4.1</c>, CDN-pinned in <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>) renders these\n72\t/// boundary-clipped subgraph edges faithfully; this was verified by rendering both the anchor\n73\t/// form and the direct form headless against 11.4.1 and measuring the edge endpoints (the anchor\n74\t/// form terminated ~65px INSIDE each box; the direct form lands ON the border). Container \"kind\"\n75\t/// styling (task / plan-level) is applied via a per-container <c>style &lt;id&gt; fill:…;</c>\n76\t/// statement rather than a <c>class &lt;id&gt; &lt;className&gt;;</c> assignment — in 11.4.1 a\n77\t/// <c>class</c> assignment does not reach a subgraph that is itself an edge endpoint (and every\n78\t/// container is one under the subgraph→subgraph model), whereas <c>style &lt;id&gt;</c> colours it\n79\t/// and also colours an EMPTY plan-level bracket (which Mermaid renders as a plain node, not a\n80\t/// cluster). Only the LEAF check nodes keep <c>classDef</c>-based colouring (<c>:::preflight</c> /\n81\t/// <c>:::guardrail</c>).\n82\t/// </para>\n83\t/// <para>\n84\t/// <b>A task container's click target is a POST-RENDER SVG overlay on its title band (issue\n85\t/// #232/#233 superseded, issue #235), NOT a Mermaid-source mechanism at all.</b> The #210 edge fix\n86\t/// above only changed how DAG EDGES attach to a container; it did not change (and never claimed to\n87\t/// change) how the container's own click target resolves. Real headless-Chrome verification against\n88\t/// the bundled <c>mermaid@11.4.1</c> — clicking the container body, its title text, and its fill\n89\t/// rect, then checking whether a real navigation (a popup) actually fired — proved a Mermaid\n90\t/// <c>click</c> directive targeting a subgraph/cluster id NEVER fires: Mermaid wraps a clickable LEAF\n91\t/// node in a real <c>&lt;a href&gt;</c> element (confirmed firing), but never wraps a\n92\t/// <c>&lt;g class=\"cluster\"&gt;</c> (subgraph) in one, regardless of what id a <c>click</c> directive\n93\t/// names. This is a genuine, still-open upstream Mermaid limitation: mermaid-js/mermaid#1637 (\"Let\n94\t/// subgraph handle clicks\") and #5428 (\"click action for subgraphs\") are both open feature requests\n95\t/// as of this writing.\n96\t/// </para>\n97\t/// <para>\n98\t/// <b>Why the first fix (#232/#233, an invisible anchor NODE) was insufficient.</b> That fix added\n99\t/// one <c>{containerId}_anchor[\" \"]:::invisible</c> node per container and pointed the container's\n100\t/// <c>click</c> directive at it instead of the subgraph id — which DOES fire (Mermaid wraps it in a\n101\t/// real <c>&lt;a href&gt;</c>, like any leaf node) but is USELESS in practice: dagre (Mermaid's layout\n102\t/// engine) sizes a <c>[\" \"]</c>-labelled node to a tiny default (~39×20px) and packs it wherever ITS\n103\t/// OWN layout algorithm decides — for a container with several guardrail leaf boxes packed\n104\t/// side-by-side, that is a thin sliver squeezed into whatever gap remains, not centered and not\n105\t/// where a user would naturally click. Measured on a real 4-guardrail task container: the anchor\n106\t/// covered 0.44% of the container's area, in a narrow strip near the container's right edge, and\n107\t/// none of 4 realistic click points (dead-center, near-title, left-margin, bottom-strip) landed on\n108\t/// it — dead-center instead landed on a leaf guardrail box's own click target and opened THAT\n109\t/// guardrail's source file instead of the task folder. Forcing the anchor wider via a padded label\n110\t/// does not fix this either (verified): dagre still packs it into its own slot rather than centering\n111\t/// or spanning it, and a content-dense container has almost no empty background region to reliably\n112\t/// overlay in the first place. This whole \"shape the anchor node's content to control its size/\n113\t/// position\" direction was abandoned as unfixable via the Mermaid-source anchor-node mechanism.\n114\t/// </para>\n115\t/// <para>\n116\t/// <b>The fix: an SVG overlay on the container's TITLE/LABEL ROW, injected via JavaScript AFTER\n117\t/// Mermaid's render completes.</b> Mermaid always renders a cluster (task container) as\n118\t/// <c>&lt;g class=\"cluster\" id=\"...\"&gt;</c> with exactly two children: a background <c>&lt;rect&gt;</c>\n119\t/// and a <c>&lt;g class=\"cluster-label\"&gt;</c> (the title text) — the label always sits in its own\n120\t/// reserved header strip ABOVE where any leaf node begins (measured on a real container: label\n121\t/// spanned y=310.06→341.4, first leaf node did not start until y=373.7 — a genuine ~32px full-width\n122\t/// gap). This band is empty BY CONSTRUCTION regardless of how many/how large a task's checks are, so\n123\t/// it is a reliable click target no matter how content-dense the container is — unlike a dagre-packed\n124\t/// interior node. <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>'s embedded script (never\n125\t/// <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/>/this Mermaid SOURCE, which stays exactly the container-model shape\n126\t/// issue #210 left it) computes, for every task container, a full-width band from the container's\n127\t/// bounding box down to just past the label's bottom edge, and appends a real\n128\t/// <c>&lt;a href=\"...\" target=\"_blank\"&gt;&lt;rect fill=\"transparent\"&gt;&lt;/a&gt;</c> covering that\n129\t/// band as the cluster group's LAST child — appended (not inserted first), so it paints ON TOP of\n130\t/// the cluster's own background rect (the cluster's only two original children) while still living\n131\t/// in a different top-level SVG group from every leaf node's own clickable <c>&lt;a&gt;</c>, so it can\n132\t/// never occlude or be occluded by a leaf-node click target. The Mermaid source contributes NO\n133\t/// anchor node, NO <c>:::invisible</c> classDef, and no <c>click</c> directive for the container at\n134\t/// all now — the task→folder path data the overlay script needs is threaded through as a small\n135\t/// embedded JSON side-table (see <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>), not a Mermaid <c>click</c>\n136\t/// directive. Leaf check-node clicks are completely unaffected — they still use Mermaid's native\n137\t/// <c>click href</c> mechanism, which already works.\n138\t/// </para>\n139\t/// <para>\n140\t/// A task-level preflight still gates its producer's <c>dependsOn</c> edge: the edge remains\n141\t/// drawn container→container exactly as any other dependency edge, and the preflight renders as an\n142\t/// ordinary check node inside the consumer's own container (before its guardrail check nodes) —\n143\t/// it is never re-routed to originate from the preflight node itself.\n144\t/// </para>\n145\t/// <para>\n146\t/// Line breaks are emitted as an explicit <c>\\n</c> (never\n147\t/// <see cref=\"StringBuilder.AppendLine()\"/>, which writes <c>Environment.NewLine</c> = CRLF\n148\t/// on Windows). This keeps <see cref=\"Render\"/>, <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/>, and the\n149\t/// <c>--stdout</c> output byte-identical on every OS, so the committed <c>diagram.md</c>\n150\t/// few-shot reference never churns between a Windows and a Linux regeneration (issue #3).\n151\t/// </para>\n152\t/// </remarks>\n153\tpublic static class MermaidRenderer\n154\t{\n155\t    private const string PlanPreflightsId = \"plan_preflights\";\n156\t    private const string PlanGuardrailsId = \"plan_guardrails\";\n157\t\n158\t    /// <summary>\n159\t    /// The legend text placed OUTSIDE the Mermaid graph (see class remarks, \"Legend lives\n160\t    /// outside the Mermaid graph\"). States both the colour mapping and the before/after timing —\n161\t    /// a bare category name would not preserve the ordering semantic the removed nested boxes used\n162\t    /// to convey visually. Consumed by <c>GraphCommand</c> (a plain Markdown block placed after the\n163\t    /// fenced <c>```mermaid```</c> block in <c>diagram.md</c>) and by <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>\n164\t    /// (rendered into the HTML overlay div for <c>diagram.html</c>). Public because both consumers\n165\t    /// live outside this assembly's <c>InternalsVisibleTo</c> set (the CLI project). Deliberately NOT\n166\t    /// part of <see cref=\"Render\"/>/<see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/>'s returned Mermaid source or\n167\t    /// <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/> — see class remarks.\n168\t    /// </summary>\n169\t    public const string LegendMarkdown =\n170\t        \"**Legend**\\n\\n\"\n171\t        + \"- 🟣 **Preflight** — verified BEFORE the task's attempt loop; gates entry \"\n172\t        + \"(dependency-delivery precondition)\\n\"\n173\t        + \"- 🟡 **Guardrail** — verified AFTER the task's action; must pass for the task to finish\\n\"\n174\t        + \"- 🟢 Plan-level containers (\\\"Full Flight Checks\\\" top, \\\"Terminal Gate\\\" bottom) run the \"\n175\t        + \"same two checks once for the whole plan, at the very start and very end.\\n\";\n176\t\n177\t    // Container fills applied per-container via a `style <id> …` statement (NOT a\n178\t    // `class <id> <className>;` statement). In Mermaid 11.4.1 a `class` assignment does NOT reach\n179\t    // a subgraph that is itself an edge endpoint — and every container is an edge endpoint under\n180\t    // the subgraph→subgraph edge model (issue #210) — whereas a `style <id>` DOES colour it. A\n181\t    // `style <id>` also colours an EMPTY plan-level bracket, which Mermaid renders as a plain node\n182\t    // rather than a cluster; that keeps the Full Flight Checks / Terminal Gate brackets on-brand\n183\t    // even when their folder is empty. Values mirror the retired `classDef task`/`classDef\n184\t    // planLevel` fills exactly, so the rendered colours are unchanged.\n185\t    private const string TaskStyle = \"fill:#cfe8ff,stroke:#1b6ec2,color:#0b2545;\";\n186\t    private const string PlanLevelStyle = \"fill:#d4edda,stroke:#2e7d32,color:#10341a;\";\n187\t\n188\t    /// <summary>Render the plan as a Mermaid <c>flowchart TD</c> string (no trailing I/O).</summary>\n189\t    public static string Render(PlanDefinition plan)\n190\t    {\n191\t        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(plan);\n192\t\n193\t        var sb = new StringBuilder();\n194\t        AppendLf(sb, \"flowchart TD\");\n195\t        AppendNodesAndEdges(plan, sb);\n196\t        AppendClassDefs(sb);\n197\t        return sb.ToString();\n198\t    }\n199\t\n200\t    /// <summary>\n201\t    /// Render the plan PLUS <c>click</c> directives that open each CHECK node's source under the\n202\t    /// plan folder (a preflight/guardrail node opens its own file — issue #33). Used ONLY for the\n203\t    /// local <c>diagram.html</c> viewer:\n204\t    /// <list type=\"bullet\">\n205\t    ///   <item>GitHub renders Mermaid in a sandboxed mode that disables clicks, so these would be\n206\t    ///         inert in <c>diagram.md</c> — and the targets are <c>file://</c>-local anyway.</item>\n207\t    ///   <item>They are deliberately NOT in <c>diagram.md</c> and NOT in the staleness hash\n208\t    ///         (<see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/>); the targets are derived deterministically from the\n209\t    ///         same plan, as plan-relative forward-slash paths, so the output is byte-identical on\n210\t    ///         every OS (no timestamp, no absolute path).</item>\n211\t    /// </list>\n212\t    /// A TASK CONTAINER's click target is NOT a Mermaid <c>click</c> directive at all (see class\n213\t    /// remarks, \"A task container's click target is a POST-RENDER SVG overlay...\" — issue\n214\t    /// #232/#233 superseded, issue #235): <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>'s embedded script injects\n215\t    /// a title-band overlay after Mermaid's render completes, using <see cref=\"TaskFolderTargets\"/>\n216\t    /// for the folder path data. This method emits no anchor node, no <c>invisible</c> classDef, and\n217\t    /// no container <c>click</c> directive — only CHECK-node clicks, identical in shape to\n218\t    /// <see cref=\"Render\"/>'s Mermaid source plus the click lines.\n219\t    /// </summary>\n220\t    public static string RenderInteractive(PlanDefinition plan)\n221\t    {\n222\t        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(plan);\n223\t\n224\t        var sb = new StringBuilder();\n225\t        AppendLf(sb, \"flowchart TD\");\n226\t        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase = AppendNodesAndEdges(plan, sb);\n227\t        AppendClassDefs(sb);\n228\t        AppendClickDirectives(plan, nodeIdBase, sb);\n229\t        return sb.ToString();\n230\t    }\n231\t\n232\t    /// <summary>\n233\t    /// The task-id → plan-relative folder path map <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/> needs to inject\n234\t    /// the title-band click overlay (see class remarks, issue #235): a task container's click target\n235\t    /// is no longer a Mermaid-source mechanism, so this is how the same path data\n236\t    /// <see cref=\"AppendClickDirectives\"/> used to feed the removed anchor's <c>click href</c> now\n237\t    /// reaches the post-render JavaScript instead — as a small embedded JSON side-table keyed by the\n238\t    /// SAME container id (<c>task_&lt;base&gt;</c>) <see cref=\"AppendTaskContainer\"/> emits, so the\n239\t    /// overlay script can look a cluster's target up by its own DOM id. Plan-relative, forward-slash\n240\t    /// paths (not OS separators, not absolute) for the same byte-identical-across-OSes reason as\n241\t    /// <see cref=\"ToPlanRelative\"/>.\n242\t    /// </summary>\n243\t    public static IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> TaskFolderTargets(PlanDefinition plan)\n244\t    {\n245\t        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(plan);\n246\t\n247\t        List<TaskNode> tasks = plan.Tasks.OrderBy(t => t.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal).ToList();\n248\t        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase = AllocateNodeIdBases(tasks);\n249\t\n250\t        var targets = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);\n251\t        foreach (TaskNode task in tasks)\n252\t        {\n253\t            string containerId = $\"task_{nodeIdBase[task.Id]}\";\n254\t            targets[containerId] = ToPlanRelative(plan.PlanDirectory, task.Directory) + \"/\";\n255\t        }\n256\t\n257\t        return targets;\n258\t    }\n259\t\n260\t    /// <summary>\n261\t    /// The cosmetic <c>classDef</c> lines (colors) for the LEAF check nodes — preflight check\n262\t    /// and guardrail check — which reference them inline via <c>:::preflight</c>/<c>:::guardrail</c>.\n263\t    /// The task-container and plan-level-container fills are applied per-container by a\n264\t    /// <c>style &lt;id&gt; …</c> statement instead (see <see cref=\"TaskStyle\"/> /\n265\t    /// <see cref=\"PlanLevelStyle\"/>), because a <c>class</c> assignment does not reach a subgraph\n266\t    /// that is an edge endpoint in the bundled Mermaid. Shared by <see cref=\"Render\"/> and\n267\t    /// <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/>; deliberately EXCLUDED from the staleness key (see\n268\t    /// <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/>), which is why <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/> does not call it.\n269\t    /// No longer emits an <c>invisible</c> classDef (issue #211's anchor-node mechanism was removed\n270\t    /// entirely — issue #235; see class remarks): the task-container click target is now a\n271\t    /// post-render SVG overlay <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/> injects via JavaScript, not a\n272\t    /// Mermaid node/class at all.\n273\t    /// </summary>\n274\t    private static void AppendClassDefs(StringBuilder sb)\n275\t    {\n276\t        AppendLf(sb, \"  classDef preflight fill:#e6d7ff,stroke:#6f42c1,color:#2e1065;\");\n277\t        AppendLf(sb, \"  classDef guardrail fill:#fff3cd,stroke:#b8860b,color:#3d2c00;\");\n278\t    }\n279\t\n280\t    /// <summary>\n281\t    /// The SEMANTIC content of the diagram: ONLY the containers + nested checks + container edges\n282\t    /// (with their drawn labels), with NO <c>flowchart TD</c> header and NO cosmetic\n283\t    /// <c>classDef</c> color definitions. This is what <see cref=\"GraphSourceHash\"/> hashes, so\n284\t    /// the staleness key tracks exactly what the diagram DRAWS (container membership, nested\n285\t    /// check labels, DAG shape) — including the PLAN-LEVEL <c>preflights/</c>/<c>guardrails/</c>\n286\t    /// folder checks, not just <c>tasks{}</c>, so editing a Terminal Gate check moves the hash\n287\t    /// too. Shares the single <see cref=\"AppendNodesAndEdges\"/> emitter with <see cref=\"Render\"/>,\n288\t    /// so the two can never drift.\n289\t    /// </summary>\n290\t    internal static string SemanticContent(PlanDefinition plan)\n291\t    {\n292\t        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(plan);\n293\t\n294\t        var sb = new StringBuilder();\n295\t        AppendNodesAndEdges(plan, sb);\n296\t        return sb.ToString();\n297\t    }\n298\t\n299\t    /// <summary>\n300\t    /// Append the container model (the semantic content) for the plan: the plan-level Full Flight\n301\t    /// Checks container, one container per task in ordinal order, the plan-level Terminal Gate\n302\t    /// container, and finally every container→container edge. The single shared emitter behind\n303\t    /// <see cref=\"Render\"/>, <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/>, and <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> —\n304\t    /// all three now emit the IDENTICAL container/node shape (issue #235 removed the interactive-only\n305\t    /// anchor node), so <see cref=\"Render\"/> and <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> differ ONLY in\n306\t    /// whether <c>click</c> directives for CHECK nodes are appended afterward. Returns the\n307\t    /// task-id → node-id-base map so the caller can emit click directives against the SAME node ids\n308\t    /// (the emitted bytes are unchanged whether or not the caller uses the return value).\n309\t    /// </summary>\n310\t    /// <remarks>\n311\t    /// ORDER MATTERS: every container is emitted (fully, including its <c>end</c>) BEFORE any\n312\t    /// container→container edge line. A <c>subgraph A --&gt; subgraph B</c> edge references the two\n313\t    /// container ids, so both subgraph blocks must already be declared; emitting all containers\n314\t    /// first keeps every edge's endpoints resolvable and the output deterministic.\n315\t    /// </remarks>\n316\t    private static IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> AppendNodesAndEdges(PlanDefinition plan, StringBuilder sb)\n317\t    {\n318\t        var graph = new DependencyGraph(plan.Tasks);\n319\t\n320\t        // Ordinal task order throughout (repo convention).\n321\t        List<TaskNode> tasks = plan.Tasks\n322\t            .OrderBy(t => t.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal)\n323\t            .ToList();\n324\t\n325\t        // Allocate an injective node-id base per task ONCE, in ordinal order: a task whose\n326\t        // sanitized id collides with an earlier one gets a deterministic _2, _3, … suffix.\n327\t        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase = AllocateNodeIdBases(tasks);\n328\t\n329\t        // --- plan-level \"Full Flight Checks\" container (top, ALWAYS emitted) -----------\n330\t        AppendPlanLevelContainer(sb, PlanPreflightsId, \"Full Flight Checks\", plan.PlanPreflights, \"preflight\");\n331\t\n332\t        // --- one container per task ------------------------------------------------------\n333\t        foreach (TaskNode task in tasks)\n334\t        {\n335\t            AppendTaskContainer(sb, task, nodeIdBase[task.Id]);\n336\t        }\n337\t\n338\t        // --- plan-level \"Terminal Gate\" container (bottom, ALWAYS emitted) --------------\n339\t        AppendPlanLevelContainer(sb, PlanGuardrailsId, \"Terminal Gate\", plan.PlanGuardrails, \"guardrail\");\n340\t\n341\t        // --- container→container edges (every container above is already fully declared) -----\n342\t        AppendContainerEdges(graph, tasks, nodeIdBase, sb);\n343\t\n344\t        return nodeIdBase;\n345\t    }\n346\t\n347\t    /// <summary>\n348\t    /// Append a plan-level bracket container (<c>plan_preflights</c> or <c>plan_guardrails</c>):\n349\t    /// its checks (sorted ordinal by name) as small boxes inside, styled with\n350\t    /// <paramref name=\"checkClass\"/>. ALWAYS emitted, even when <paramref name=\"checks\"/> is empty\n351\t    /// — the two plan-level containers are structural brackets on the whole DAG, not conditional\n352\t    /// content. The DAG edge attaches to this container's own subgraph id (no interior anchor).\n353\t    /// </summary>\n354\t    private static void AppendPlanLevelContainer(\n355\t        StringBuilder sb,\n356\t        string containerId,\n357\t        string label,\n358\t        IReadOnlyList<GuardrailDefinition> checks,\n359\t        string checkClass)\n360\t    {\n361\t        AppendLf(sb, $\"  subgraph {containerId}[{Quote(label)}]\");\n362\t        AppendCheckNodes(sb, \"    \", $\"{containerId}\", checks, checkClass);\n363\t        AppendLf(sb, \"  end\");\n364\t        AppendLf(sb, $\"  style {containerId} {PlanLevelStyle}\");\n365\t    }\n366\t\n367\t    /// <summary>\n368\t    /// Append one task container: its preflight leaf check node(s) (if any), THEN its guardrail\n369\t    /// leaf check node(s) — both DIRECTLY inside the container, with no nested\n370\t    /// <c>Preflights</c>/<c>Guardrails</c> wrapper subgraph (see class remarks, \"Nested boxes\n371\t    /// dropped\") — then the container's <c>style</c> fill. The DAG edge attaches to this\n372\t    /// container's own subgraph id (no interior anchor).\n373\t    /// </summary>\n374\t    /// <remarks>\n375\t    /// <b>Emission-order contract (load-bearing, tested):</b> preflight check nodes are ALWAYS\n376\t    /// emitted before guardrail check nodes within a container. This is not a rendering accident —\n377\t    /// with the nested boxes gone, source order is the only surviving signal that preflights run\n378\t    /// BEFORE the task's attempt loop and guardrails run AFTER it, so callers (and the legend) may\n379\t    /// rely on it as a stable convention.\n380\t    /// </remarks>\n381\t    /// <remarks>\n382\t    /// No anchor node of any kind is emitted here (issue #211's mechanism was removed entirely —\n383\t    /// issue #235; see class remarks). <see cref=\"Render\"/> and <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> now\n384\t    /// emit byte-identical container/node shape for every task; the container's click target lives\n385\t    /// entirely in <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>'s post-render JavaScript overlay instead.\n386\t    /// </remarks>\n387\t    private static void AppendTaskContainer(StringBuilder sb, TaskNode task, string @base)\n388\t    {\n389\t        string containerId = $\"task_{@base}\";\n390\t\n391\t        AppendLf(sb, $\"  subgraph {containerId}[{Quote(task.Id)}]\");\n392\t\n393\t        // Preflights BEFORE guardrails — see remarks: this order is the emission-order contract\n394\t        // that now carries the \"before the attempt loop\" / \"after the action\" temporal semantic\n395\t        // the removed nested boxes used to convey visually.\n396\t        AppendCheckNodes(sb, \"    \", $\"{containerId}_pf\", task.Preflights, \"preflight\");\n397\t        AppendCheckNodes(sb, \"    \", $\"{containerId}_gr\", task.Guardrails, \"guardrail\");\n398\t\n399\t        AppendLf(sb, \"  end\");\n400\t        AppendLf(sb, $\"  style {containerId} {TaskStyle}\");\n401\t    }\n402\t\n403\t    /// <summary>\n404\t    /// Append <paramref name=\"checks\"/> (sorted ordinal by name, for input-order independence) as\n405\t    /// <c>{nodeIdPrefix}_{ordinal}[label]:::{checkClass}</c> node lines, one per check. Drawn label\n406\t    /// is ALWAYS <see cref=\"GuardrailDefinition.Name\"/> — the check's own short, stable identifier\n407\t    /// (the file-derived name, e.g. <c>01-core-tests-green-excluding-target</c>), never the\n408\t    /// (possibly long) <see cref=\"GuardrailDefinition.Description\"/>. A prior version drew the\n409\t    /// description (truncated for task-level preflights only, issue #211) — the owner asked\n410\t    /// instead for the same short, meaningful identifier every box's click target already opens,\n411\t    /// uniformly for every check kind at both scopes (issue #222). The full description remains\n412\t    /// reachable via the node's <c>click</c> tooltip in <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> (issue\n413\t    /// #33's existing click mechanism, unaffected by this change) — no truncation heuristic is\n414\t    /// needed anywhere now.\n415\t    /// </summary>\n416\t    private static void AppendCheckNodes(\n417\t        StringBuilder sb,\n418\t        string indent,\n419\t        string nodeIdPrefix,\n420\t        IReadOnlyList<GuardrailDefinition> checks,\n421\t        string checkClass)\n422\t    {\n423\t        int ordinal = 0;\n424\t        foreach (GuardrailDefinition check in checks.OrderBy(c => c.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n425\t        {\n426\t            AppendLf(sb, $\"{indent}{nodeIdPrefix}_{ordinal}[{Quote(check.Name)}]:::{checkClass}\");\n427\t            ordinal++;\n428\t        }\n429\t    }\n430\t\n431\t    /// <summary>\n432\t    /// Append every container→container edge: the plan-preflights container into each DAG ROOT\n433\t    /// task's container (a task with no <c>dependsOn</c>), one edge per <c>dependsOn</c>\n434\t    /// relationship between two task containers, and each DAG LEAF task's container (a task nothing\n435\t    /// depends on) into the plan-guardrails container. The edge references the container's own\n436\t    /// subgraph id, so Mermaid clips the arrow to the container's OUTER BORDER (issue #210). A\n437\t    /// task-level preflight does not change this — the gated dependency edge is drawn exactly like\n438\t    /// any other; the preflight is only ever a check node inside the consumer's own container\n439\t    /// (emitted before the container's guardrail check nodes — see <see cref=\"AppendTaskContainer\"/>).\n440\t    /// </summary>\n441\t    private static void AppendContainerEdges(\n442\t        DependencyGraph graph,\n443\t        IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks,\n444\t        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase,\n445\t        StringBuilder sb)\n446\t    {\n447\t        foreach (TaskNode root in tasks.Where(t => t.DependsOn.Count == 0))\n448\t        {\n449\t            AppendLf(sb, $\"  {PlanPreflightsId} --> task_{nodeIdBase[root.Id]}\");\n450\t        }\n451\t\n452\t        foreach (TaskNode dependency in tasks)\n453\t        {\n454\t            foreach (string dependentId in graph.DependentsOf(dependency.Id)\n455\t                         .OrderBy(id => id, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n456\t            {\n457\t                AppendLf(sb, $\"  task_{nodeIdBase[dependency.Id]} --> task_{nodeIdBase[dependentId]}\");\n458\t            }\n459\t        }\n460\t\n461\t        foreach (TaskNode leaf in tasks.Where(t => graph.DependentsOf(t.Id).Count == 0))\n462\t        {\n463\t            AppendLf(sb, $\"  task_{nodeIdBase[leaf.Id]} --> {PlanGuardrailsId}\");\n464\t        }\n465\t    }\n466\t\n467\t    /// <summary>\n468\t    /// Append <c>click</c> directives (HTML-viewer only; see <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/>) for\n469\t    /// every CHECK node — plan-level or task-level, preflight or guardrail — opening its own file\n470\t    /// as a plan-relative, forward-slash <c>file://</c> target resolved relative to\n471\t    /// <c>diagram.html</c> at the plan root, opened in a new tab (<c>_blank</c>) so the diagram\n472\t    /// stays put. Emitted in the same ordinal/sorted order as the nodes for determinism, and using\n473\t    /// the SAME node-id scheme as <see cref=\"AppendNodesAndEdges\"/> so every click target actually\n474\t    /// exists. A task-level preflight's click tooltip carries its FULL description (not just its\n475\t    /// name) since <see cref=\"AppendCheckNodes\"/> draws only a truncated label for it — the\n476\t    /// tooltip is the click-for-detail mechanism that keeps the full text from being lost.\n477\t    /// </summary>\n478\t    /// <remarks>\n479\t    /// <b>No container click directive is emitted here (issue #235).</b> A task container's click\n480\t    /// target is no longer a Mermaid mechanism at all — see class remarks, \"A task container's click\n481\t    /// target is a POST-RENDER SVG overlay...\". <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/> injects it via\n482\t    /// JavaScript after Mermaid's render completes, using <see cref=\"TaskFolderTargets\"/> for the\n483\t    /// folder path data. Leaf check-node clicks are unaffected here: they still target the leaf node\n484\t    /// itself, which Mermaid DOES wrap in a real clickable <c>&lt;a href&gt;</c>.\n485\t    /// </remarks>\n486\t    private static void AppendClickDirectives(\n487\t        PlanDefinition plan, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase, StringBuilder sb)\n488\t    {\n489\t        AppendCheckClicks(plan, plan.PlanPreflights, PlanPreflightsId, sb);\n490\t\n491\t        foreach (TaskNode task in plan.Tasks.OrderBy(t => t.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n492\t        {\n493\t            string @base = nodeIdBase[task.Id];\n494\t            string containerId = $\"task_{@base}\";\n495\t\n496\t            if (task.Preflights.Count > 0)\n497\t            {\n498\t                AppendCheckClicks(plan, task.Preflights, $\"{containerId}_pf\", sb);\n499\t            }\n500\t\n501\t            AppendCheckClicks(plan, task.Guardrails, $\"{containerId}_gr\", sb);\n502\t        }\n503\t\n504\t        AppendCheckClicks(plan, plan.PlanGuardrails, PlanGuardrailsId, sb);\n505\t    }\n506\t\n507\t    /// <summary>\n508\t    /// Append one <c>click</c> directive per check in <paramref name=\"checks\"/> (sorted ordinal by\n509\t    /// name, mirroring <see cref=\"AppendCheckNodes\"/> exactly so the ordinal-suffixed node id each\n510\t    /// click targets is the one actually emitted for that check). The tooltip is ALWAYS\n511\t    /// <c>Description ?? Name</c> in full, for every check kind at both scopes — since the drawn\n512\t    /// label is now always the short <c>Name</c> (issue #222), the tooltip is the one place the\n513\t    /// full description lives; there is no longer a \"some checks get the full text, others don't\"\n514\t    /// distinction.\n515\t    /// </summary>\n516\t    private static void AppendCheckClicks(\n517\t        PlanDefinition plan,\n518\t        IReadOnlyList<GuardrailDefinition> checks,\n519\t        string nodeIdPrefix,\n520\t        StringBuilder sb)\n521\t    {\n522\t        int ordinal = 0;\n523\t        foreach (GuardrailDefinition check in checks.OrderBy(c => c.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n524\t        {\n525\t            string checkPath = ToPlanRelative(plan.PlanDirectory, check.Path);\n526\t            string tooltipText = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(check.Description) ? check.Name : check.Description!;\n527\t            AppendLf(sb, $\"  click {nodeIdPrefix}_{ordinal} href \\\"{checkPath}\\\" \\\"{ClickTooltip(tooltipText)}\\\" _blank\");\n528\t            ordinal++;\n529\t        }\n530\t    }\n531\t\n532\t    /// <summary>\n533\t    /// A plan-folder-relative, forward-slash path for a <c>click href</c> target. Forward slashes\n534\t    /// (not OS separators) keep the generated <c>diagram.html</c> byte-identical across OSes and\n535\t    /// make the href resolve relative to <c>diagram.html</c> at the plan root.\n536\t    /// </summary>\n537\t    private static string ToPlanRelative(string planDirectory, string absolutePath) =>\n538\t        Path.GetRelativePath(planDirectory, absolutePath)\n539\t            .Replace('\\\\', '/')\n540\t            .Replace(\"\\\"\", \"%22\", StringComparison.Ordinal); // \" is legal in Linux filenames; URL-encode to keep the click directive parseable\n541\t\n542\t    /// <summary>\n543\t    /// Make a label safe inside a double-quoted Mermaid <c>click</c> tooltip: collapse any line\n544\t    /// break to a space (a <c>click</c> directive is line-oriented, so a raw newline — now\n545\t    /// possible here since a task-level preflight's tooltip can carry its full, sometimes\n546\t    /// multi-line, description — would silently truncate or corrupt the directive) and escape\n547\t    /// embedded double quotes.\n548\t    /// </summary>\n549\t    private static string ClickTooltip(string text) =>\n550\t        text\n551\t            .Replace(\"\\r\\n\", \" \", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n552\t            .Replace(\"\\r\", \" \", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n553\t            .Replace(\"\\n\", \" \", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n554\t            .Replace(\"\\\"\", \"&quot;\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n555\t\n556\t    /// <summary>\n557\t    /// Append <paramref name=\"line\"/> followed by an explicit <c>'\\n'</c>. Used everywhere a\n558\t    /// line is emitted INSTEAD of <see cref=\"StringBuilder.AppendLine(string)\"/>, whose\n559\t    /// <c>Environment.NewLine</c> would inject CRLF on Windows and make the rendered diagram\n560\t    /// (and its source hash) platform-dependent (issue #3).\n561\t    /// </summary>\n562\t    private static void AppendLf(StringBuilder sb, string line) => sb.Append(line).Append('\\n');\n563\t\n564\t    // --- node id helpers --------------------------------------------------------------\n565\t\n566\t    /// <summary>\n567\t    /// Build the task-id → node-id-base map for <paramref name=\"tasks\"/> (already ordinal),\n568\t    /// guaranteeing distinct bases even when two task ids <see cref=\"Sanitize\"/> to the same\n569\t    /// string (e.g. <c>a.b</c> and <c>a_b</c> both → <c>a_b</c>). The first claimant keeps the\n570\t    /// readable sanitized base; later collisions get a deterministic <c>_2</c>, <c>_3</c>, …\n571\t    /// suffix in ordinal order. Every node/container family for a task (the container itself and\n572\t    /// its preflight/guardrail check nodes) derives from this unique base, so all ids stay\n573\t    /// collision-free. Also used by <see cref=\"TaskFolderTargets\"/> so its JSON side-table is keyed\n574\t    /// by the SAME container id this method produces for <see cref=\"AppendNodesAndEdges\"/>.\n575\t    /// </summary>\n576\t    private static IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> AllocateNodeIdBases(IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks)\n577\t    {\n578\t        var bases = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);\n579\t        var taken = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);\n580\t\n581\t        foreach (TaskNode task in tasks)\n582\t        {\n583\t            string candidate = Sanitize(task.Id);\n584\t            if (!taken.Add(candidate))\n585\t            {\n586\t                int suffix = 2;\n587\t                string disambiguated;\n588\t                do\n589\t                {\n590\t                    disambiguated = $\"{candidate}_{suffix}\";\n591\t                    suffix++;\n592\t                }\n593\t                while (!taken.Add(disambiguated));\n594\t\n595\t                candidate = disambiguated;\n596\t            }\n597\t\n598\t            bases[task.Id] = candidate;\n599\t        }\n600\t\n601\t        return bases;\n602\t    }\n603\t\n604\t    /// <summary>\n605\t    /// Turn an id into a safe Mermaid node-id fragment: every character that is not an ASCII\n606\t    /// letter, digit, or underscore becomes <c>_</c> (so kebab <c>-</c> → <c>_</c>). Because\n607\t    /// this is many-to-one (e.g. <c>a.b</c> and <c>a_b</c> both map to <c>a_b</c>),\n608\t    /// <see cref=\"AllocateNodeIdBases\"/> deduplicates the results so node ids stay injective.\n609\t    /// </summary>\n610\t    private static string Sanitize(string id)\n611\t    {\n612\t        var sb = new StringBuilder(id.Length);\n613\t        foreach (char c in id)\n614\t        {\n615\t            bool safe = c is (>= 'a' and <= 'z') or (>= 'A' and <= 'Z') or (>= '0' and <= '9');\n616\t            sb.Append(safe ? c : '_');\n617\t        }\n618\t\n619\t        return sb.ToString();\n620\t    }\n621\t\n622\t    /// <summary>\n623\t    /// Wrap a label in double quotes for a Mermaid node and make free-text descriptions safe.\n624\t    /// Mermaid flowchart syntax is line-oriented and renders labels as HTML, so a raw label\n625\t    /// can break the WHOLE diagram. This (1) collapses every line break (<c>\\r\\n</c>, <c>\\r</c>,\n626\t    /// <c>\\n</c>) to a single space, then (2) HTML-escapes in an order that never double-escapes\n627\t    /// entities: <c>&amp;</c>→<c>&amp;amp;</c>, <c>&lt;</c>→<c>&amp;lt;</c>, <c>&gt;</c>→\n628\t    /// <c>&amp;gt;</c>, <c>\"</c>→<c>&amp;quot;</c>, <c>#</c>→<c>&amp;#35;</c> (<c>&lt;</c>/<c>&gt;</c>\n629\t    /// would otherwise silently drop text as stray tags; <c>#</c> can trigger entity parsing).\n630\t    /// </summary>\n631\t    private static string Quote(string label)\n632\t    {\n633\t        string collapsed = label\n634\t            .Replace(\"\\r\\n\", \" \", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n635\t            .Replace(\"\\r\", \" \", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n636\t            .Replace(\"\\n\", \" \", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n637\t\n638\t        string escaped = collapsed\n639\t            .Replace(\"&\", \"&amp;\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n640\t            .Replace(\"<\", \"&lt;\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n641\t            .Replace(\">\", \"&gt;\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n642\t            .Replace(\"\\\"\", \"&quot;\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n643\t            .Replace(\"#\", \"&#35;\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n644\t\n645\t        return \"\\\"\" + escaped + \"\\\"\";\n646\t    }\n647\t}\n648\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7f063076-33be-40ca-94ba-98c9a68db4ee","uuid":"8fbdba83-a7c3-4bb7-8614-3b17564004e2","timestamp":"2026-07-07T16:47:47.712Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\David\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\guardrails-worktrees\\diagram-live-status-and-search-80c8913d\\1bb6c1ff\\07-author-tests-diagram-search-box\\attempt-1\\src\\Guardrails.Core\\Graph\\MermaidRenderer.cs","content":"using System.Text;\nusing Guardrails.Core.Model;\n\nnamespace Guardrails.Core.Graph;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// Renders a plan's task/guardrail DAG as a Mermaid <c>flowchart TD</c> (SSOT §10) using the\n/// CONTAINER model (design-of-record 09-preflight-first-class). Pure: <see cref=\"Render\"/> maps\n/// a <see cref=\"PlanDefinition\"/> to Mermaid text with no I/O.\n/// </summary>\n/// <remarks>\n/// <para>\n/// Shape: each task is a <c>subgraph task_&lt;id&gt;</c> container holding its check nodes\n/// (preflight and guardrail leaves) DIRECTLY inside the container — no nested\n/// <c>Preflights</c>/<c>Guardrails</c> wrapper subgraph, no free guardrail/preflight nodes outside\n/// a container, no per-task <c>done_&lt;id&gt;</c> reconvergence node, no <c>task --&gt; guardrail</c>\n/// fan-out edge. (A per-task nested-subgraph wrapper was tried and dropped — see \"Nested boxes\n/// dropped\" below.) Two mandatory plan-level containers bracket the whole DAG: <c>plan_preflights</c>\n/// (\"Full Flight Checks\") at the top, <c>plan_guardrails</c> (\"Terminal Gate\") at the bottom —\n/// always emitted, even when their folder is empty, because they are structural brackets, not\n/// conditional content. These two stay titled subgraphs (unaffected by the nested-box removal\n/// below): they are one-off heterogeneous brackets on the whole DAG, not a per-task repeated\n/// pattern.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Nested boxes dropped (simplification).</b> A task container previously nested a\n/// \"Guardrails\" sub-container (and, when present, a \"Preflights\" sub-container) around its leaf\n/// check nodes — nesting-within-nesting that made a real generated diagram look busy for no\n/// semantic gain: the wrapper subgraph id was never referenced by edge emission, container\n/// styling, or <see cref=\"GraphSourceHash\"/> — purely cosmetic. Leaf check nodes are now emitted\n/// as direct children of the task container; the existing <c>:::preflight</c>/<c>:::guardrail</c>\n/// <c>classDef</c> fill remains the only visual category distinction. Removing the boxes also\n/// removes their visual \"preflights run before, guardrails run after\" cue, so that temporal fact\n/// is now preserved two other ways: (1) a GUARANTEED emission-order contract — a task's preflight\n/// leaf node(s), if any, are always emitted before its guardrail leaf node(s) within the\n/// container (see <see cref=\"AppendTaskContainer\"/>), so position is a stable, tested convention,\n/// not a rendering accident; and (2) the legend (see <see cref=\"LegendMarkdown\"/>) states the\n/// before/after timing in words, not just a bare colour-category name.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Legend lives outside the Mermaid graph.</b> A Mermaid-native legend (a disconnected\n/// subgraph of dummy colour-swatch nodes) was prototyped and rendered BROKEN headless against the\n/// exact bundled <c>mermaid@11.4.1</c>: dagre lays out a disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra\n/// \"task\" overlapping the real DAG. The only approach that renders correctly is content OUTSIDE\n/// the Mermaid source entirely: an HTML overlay `&lt;div&gt;` in <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>\n/// for <c>diagram.html</c>, and the shared <see cref=\"LegendMarkdown\"/> block placed by the CLI's\n/// <c>graph</c> command AFTER the fenced <c>```mermaid```</c> block for <c>diagram.md</c> (GitHub's\n/// Mermaid sandbox has no overlay option). Neither destination is part of <see cref=\"Render\"/>'s or\n/// <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/>'s returned Mermaid source, and — same treatment as the existing\n/// cosmetic <c>classDef</c> color lines (added by those two methods, never by\n/// <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/>) — the legend never reaches <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/> either,\n/// so legend-only wording changes never move <see cref=\"GraphSourceHash\"/> and never make\n/// `graph --check` spuriously report a plan stale.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Every check node's drawn label is its short, stable <c>Name</c> — never its (possibly long)\n/// <c>Description</c>.</b> A prior version drew a task-level preflight's full descriptive text\n/// (which can run to many words) and truncated it to fit; the owner asked instead for the same\n/// short, meaningful identifier the node's own click target already opens, uniformly for every\n/// check kind at both scopes (issue #222) — so no truncation heuristic is needed anywhere. The\n/// full <see cref=\"GuardrailDefinition.Description\"/> remains reachable via the SAME\n/// <c>click</c>-directive mechanism <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> already uses for every node\n/// (source-file click-through, issue #33) — the tooltip argument of that directive carries the\n/// full text for every check, so no new mechanism was introduced.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// The DAG is drawn <c>subgraph --&gt; subgraph</c>: each edge references a container's subgraph\n/// id directly (<c>task_A --&gt; task_B</c>, <c>plan_preflights --&gt; task_root</c>, …), so Mermaid\n/// clips the arrow to the container's OUTER BORDER like any ordinary box-to-box flowchart edge —\n/// no interior anchor, no line piercing the box (issue #210). The bundled Mermaid version\n/// (<c>mermaid@11.4.1</c>, CDN-pinned in <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>) renders these\n/// boundary-clipped subgraph edges faithfully; this was verified by rendering both the anchor\n/// form and the direct form headless against 11.4.1 and measuring the edge endpoints (the anchor\n/// form terminated ~65px INSIDE each box; the direct form lands ON the border). Container \"kind\"\n/// styling (task / plan-level) is applied via a per-container <c>style &lt;id&gt; fill:…;</c>\n/// statement rather than a <c>class &lt;id&gt; &lt;className&gt;;</c> assignment — in 11.4.1 a\n/// <c>class</c> assignment does not reach a subgraph that is itself an edge endpoint (and every\n/// container is one under the subgraph→subgraph model), whereas <c>style &lt;id&gt;</c> colours it\n/// and also colours an EMPTY plan-level bracket (which Mermaid renders as a plain node, not a\n/// cluster).
